subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should maintainers keep this as the canonical Windows gateway-down umbrella and split separate fixes for lifecycle, invalid-config repair, Browser plugin isolation, pricing readiness, and CLI backend spawning?
rationale: The report combines several credible failures across stable core gateway and CLI surfaces plus Native Windows-specific behavior, and the right split/order needs owner prioritization and live Windows proof before autonomous implementation.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
options.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow maintainer-owned fixes for each proven sub-boundary, starting with live Windows proof for lifecycle and browser crash behavior.

options.title: Require live Windows proof first
options.body: Pause code changes until a maintainer or reporter captures process, listener, browser, and startup timing proof for the highest-risk Windows paths.

options.title: Track only remaining sub-issues
options.body: Close or mark any current-main-fixed sub-branches after proof, then move the still-failing pieces into narrower follow-up issues.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow maintainer-owned fixes for each proven sub-boundary, starting with live Windows proof for lifecycle and browser crash behavior.
